limits: Three runs are not judged: paddockcore at medium, extra-high and max. A safety classifier stopped each session while the model probed the legacy binary, and it ended with an empty patch. They count as failed tasks and are priced and timed.

Max codeccore has no published Code quality score: Grok 4.6's intent probe gave no valid answer after the single retry (attempt 1 quoted a line absent from the run; attempt 2 was not valid JSON). The run passed its tests and counts as passed.

One operator recovery: Grok 4.6's primary review of extra-high vaultcore quoted a hard-wrapped line joined into one on both attempts; the standing recover_excerpts rule selected attempt 1 with the quote re-wrapped, scores untouched. Invalid-response retries under the frozen rule: Muse Spark 1.3 9, Grok 4.6 5.

Claude Code versions: low 22 on 2.1.293 and 1 on 2.1.294; medium 3 on 2.1.294 and 20 on 2.1.295; high on 2.1.295; extra-high 2 on 2.1.295 and 21 on 2.1.296; max on 2.1.296. Earlier Claude columns used older Claude Code releases.

Judge settings are the recovered original v3.3 and v3.4 protocols; Muse Spark 1.3 ran the same binary; Grok 4.6 ran through Cursor CLI 2026.10.01-e373342, pinned by version for the whole round, the same CLI that judged Sonnet 5.5. Cursor reports the display name "Grok 4.6 Medium" (frozen: "Cursor Grok 4.6 Medium"), a rename the wrapper accepted and recorded 426 times.

The sweep was stopped between tasks twice, 2026-10-09 15:43 to 2026-10-10 09:20 UTC and 2026-10-10 19:48 to 2026-10-11 15:50 UTC; no run was in progress across either pause, so run timings are intact. The host's clock moved from PDT to CEST during the sweep; all times here are UTC.
Frontier Code quality is the reviewed layer plus intent recovery and is never compared with Routine v1 Code quality.

One attempt per task and level. The sweep ran 2026-10-08 10:40 to 2026-10-11 22:49 UTC on the owner's Mac, local sandbox, flat 3-hour task bound, one task at a time. Judging ran 2026-10-11 22:52 to 2026-10-12 10:11 UTC with no sweep running.
